name: Battle of Carrhae

phases.title: The Romans form a hollow square
phases.text: Cassius advised a line with infantry in the centre and cavalry on the wings. Crassus at first agreed, then changed his mind and redeployed his men into a hollow square, each side formed by twelve cohorts.

phases.title: The cataphracts show their armour
phases.text: The Parthians beat hollow drums, and Surena ordered his cataphracts to cover their armour in cloths and advance. Within sight of the Romans they dropped the cloths together and showed their shining armour.

phases.title: Horse archers surround the square
phases.text: Surena sent his horse archers round the Roman square, beyond the range of the pila. Crassus sent his skirmishers out to drive them off, and the archers' arrows drove the skirmishers back.

phases.title: The horse archers shoot into the square
phases.text: The horse archers then engaged the legionaries. The legionaries' large shields and armour could not cover the whole body, and arrows struck them as the archers circled the square.

phases.title: The Romans advance and the archers withdraw
phases.text: The Romans repeatedly advanced towards the Parthians to fight at close quarters. The horse archers always retreated safely and shot as they withdrew.

phases.title: The cataphracts charge the testudo
phases.text: The legionaries locked their shields in the testudo, which limited their fighting in melee. The cataphracts repeatedly charged the line, and when the Romans loosened their formation the cataphracts drew back and the horse archers shot again.

phases.title: Crassus sends Publius against the archers
phases.text: Crassus hoped his men could hold out until the Parthians ran out of arrows, but camels resupplied the horse archers. He then dispatched his son Publius with Gallic cavalry, archers and eight cohorts to drive them off.

phases.title: Publius is drawn away
phases.text: The horse archers feigned retreat and drew Publius away from the main army. His force suffered heavy casualties from arrow fire as it followed.

phases.title: Publius's force is cut off on a hill
phases.text: Once Publius was well apart from the army, the cataphracts confronted his force and the horse archers cut off its retreat. The Gauls retreated to a hill, where Publius and his officers killed themselves. Only 500 Gauls were taken alive.

phases.title: Crassus orders a general advance
phases.text: Crassus did not know his son's fate but saw that Publius was in danger, and ordered a general advance. He was then shown his son's head on a spear.

phases.title: The Parthians attack until nightfall
phases.text: The horse archers began to surround the Roman infantry and shot at them from all directions. The cataphracts mounted a series of charges that disorganised the Romans, and the onslaught went on until nightfall.

phases.title: The retreat towards Carrhae
phases.text: Crassus ordered a disorganised, ragged retreat to the town of Carrhae. He left behind 4,000 wounded, who were killed by the Parthians the next morning.

phases.title: Four cohorts are lost on a hill
phases.text: Four Roman cohorts lost their way in the dark and were surrounded on a hill by the Parthians. Only 20 Romans survived.

note: The accounts do not give the compass directions, the width of the stream or where the hills and the town of Carrhae lay, so these are placed on the side the story needs and the plan is schematic. The Roman force is drawn as one hollow square although each side was formed by twelve cohorts. The date is given as 9 June by Ovid.
